narrative:
The model determined that you have a 52% chance of being a bad credit risk. Because this probability is just over the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

Three pieces of information about you weighed most heavily in this decision. First, the size of your savings account worked strongly in your favor. Having more than 1,000 DM puts you in a small and financially stable group compared with most approved applicants, who usually have far less saved. This factor pushed the prediction noticeably toward approval.

Unfortunately, two other details pulled the outcome in the opposite direction and proved more influential overall. The fact that you are requesting the loan to buy a new car increased the risk score. Among approved applicants, new-car loans are relatively uncommon; most successful applications are for other purposes such as home electronics or furniture. In addition, the current status of your checking account added further concern. An account showing between 0 and 200 DM is less reassuring to the model than the “no checking account” or “salary account” situations that dominate the approved group.

Taken together, the positive effect of your solid savings was outweighed by the combination of the new-car purpose and your checking-account balance, tipping the final prediction just above the denial line.

You should focus on two practical next steps: build a larger buffer in your checking account and consider whether a different loan purpose or a co-signer might change the risk picture. Once those areas improve, reapplying could produce a different result. (248 words)
